title: Biotech news from around the world - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A two-item news brief: Merck KGaA is acquiring US life-science reagent and instrument maker Bio-Techne for $11.3 billion to build an end-to-end discovery-through-commercial-manufacturing toolchain, and Pakistan has amended its biosafety rules to loosen GMO governance, including scrapping a 2024 sunset clause that had capped GMO imports until January 2027.

insights.claim: Merck KGaA is acquiring Bio-Techne, a US reagent and instrument maker, for $11.3 billion, one of the largest life-science tools transactions and a bet on picks-and-shovels rather than therapeutics.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: An $11.3bn print sets a valuation marker for the reagents and instruments sector and puts remaining independent toolmakers in play.
insights.quote: Merck KGaA buys US reagent and instrument maker Bio-Techne for $11.3 billion.

insights.claim: The strategic logic of the Bio-Techne purchase is vertical coverage of the customer's entire lifecycle — discovery and translational research through development, testing and commercial manufacturing — rather than a product-line bolt-on.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Full-workflow lock-in is the tools industry's moat strategy; it raises switching costs and pressures single-stage vendors.
insights.quote: allowing the combined company to support customers from discovery and translational research through development, testing and commercial manufacturing

insights.claim: Multiomics product lines are being treated as an acquirable strategic asset by a large European chemicals and life-science group, signalling that omics instrumentation has moved from research novelty to infrastructure worth paying a premium for.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Watch smaller multiomics and spatial-biology vendors as the next consolidation targets.

insights.claim: Pakistan has approved amendments to its biosafety rules that simplify GMO licensing, ease import restrictions and facilitate research, explicitly reorienting the framework toward a science-based and business-friendly regime.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A large agricultural import market opening to GMOs expands addressable demand for seed and trait developers.
insights.quote: Regulators approve amendments to Pakistan’s biosafety rules to update the GMO regulatory framework towards a science-based and business-friendly governance system.

insights.claim: The amendments remove a 2024 sunset clause that had capped Pakistan's GMO imports until January 2027, eliminating a hard regulatory cliff that had been sitting in importers' forward planning.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Removal of a dated import cap is the concrete, tradeable detail — it changes volume assumptions for agricultural biotech supply into Pakistan ahead of 2027.
insights.quote: remove the 2024 ‘sunset clause’ that previously capped GMO imports until January 2027
